text: An early price estimate pulls a later estimate toward it. Which bias is at work?
After vivid news coverage, a rare hazard feels common. Which shortcut explains this?
A person seeks only evidence that supports a prior belief. Which bias is this?
After learning an outcome, someone claims it was obvious all along. Which bias is this?
A choice changes when identical outcomes are described as gains versus losses. Which effect is this?
A person dislikes losing $20 more than they enjoy gaining $20. Which tendency is this?
Someone keeps funding a failing project because of money already spent. Which effect is this?
A person values a mug more once it belongs to them. Which effect is this?
People stick with an existing arrangement mainly because it is familiar. Which bias fits?
A small reward today is chosen over a larger reward next month. Which tendency fits?
A vivid personality sketch outweighs population frequencies in a judgment. Which shortcut fits?
Someone ignores how common a condition is when interpreting a test result. Which error is this?
A detailed two-event story seems likelier than one of its component events. Which fallacy is this?
After five heads in a row, someone thinks tails is now due from a fair coin. Which fallacy?
A lucky beginner's next score moves closer to average. What statistical pattern is this?
Only successful companies are studied, hiding the failed ones. Which bias is this?
A single admirable trait makes every trait of a person seem admirable. Which effect?
A single disliked trait colors judgment of unrelated traits. Which effect?
Someone assumes their own opinion is much more common than it is. Which effect?
Repeatedly seeing a neutral logo makes it more likable. Which effect?
A vacation is remembered mostly by its high point and ending. Which rule?
Items at the end of a list are recalled especially well. Which effect?
Items at the start of a list are recalled especially well. Which effect?
A person predicts an overly rosy personal future despite contrary data. Which bias?
One harsh review outweighs several kind reviews in someone's judgment. Which bias?
Someone credits success to skill but blames failure on bad luck. Which bias?
A driver blames their own mistake on traffic but another's on poor character. Which effect?
A stranger's lateness is blamed on personality rather than circumstances. Which error?
A team favors its own members over equally qualified outsiders. Which bias?
Members of another group seem more alike than members of one's own. Which effect?
People follow a crowd's choice as evidence of what is best. Which influence?
A group suppresses dissent to preserve harmony and reaches a poor decision. Which pattern?
An emergency witness does less because many other witnesses are present. Which effect?
A person feels less personally responsible when many others are present. Which pattern?
A limited-time label makes an ordinary item seem more desirable. Which cue?
People judge a harmful action more harshly than an equally harmful inaction. Which bias?
Adding a weak third option shifts preference between two original options. Which effect?
A preset selection gets chosen more often simply because it is preselected. Which effect?
Someone strongly favors an immediate pleasure despite long-term costs. Which bias?
A person is more certain of an answer than their accuracy warrants. Which bias?
A task is predicted to take two hours despite many past delays. Which fallacy?
Someone judges a decision solely by how it turned out, not what was known then. Which bias?
A person with limited skill overestimates their ability in that skill. Which effect?
Too many product options leave a shopper unable to decide. Which phenomenon?
A person treats random dice throws as if their own technique controls them. Which illusion?
An expert forgets how little a beginner knows when explaining a topic. Which bias?
A person thinks everyone notices a small stain on their shirt. Which effect?
An impressive job title makes an unrelated claim seem more credible. Which bias?
A familiar statement feels truer after repeated exposure. Which effect?
A team member works less hard on a group project than alone. Which pattern?
